facts.statement: Indosaurus lived in what is now India between 69 and 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Indosaurus () is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now India, about 69 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian division of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The holotype of Indosaurus was discovered between 1917 and 1919 in Jabalpur, India, by Charles Alfred Matley.
facts.quote: The now-lost holotype was discovered between 1917 and 1919 in Jabalpur, India (GSI K27/565), by Charles Alfred Matley.

facts.statement: Indosaurus matleyi was named by Huene and Matley in 1933, making it the first majungasaurine discovered.
facts.quote: The type species, Indosaurus matleyi, was named by Huene and Matley in 1933 making Indosaurus the first majungasaurine to be discovered.
The species I. matleyi weighed roughly 700 kg.

facts.statement: Indosaurus was a predator approximately 700 kilograms in weight and 6 meters long, with a large skull that likely possessed characteristic ornaments rather than horns like Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: Indosaurus era un depredador de aproximadamente 700 kilogramos de peso y alrededor de 6 metros de largo, con un cráneo de gran tamaño que probablemente poseía adornos que, si bien no llegaban a ser cuernos como en el Carnotaurus, eran característicos del clado.

facts.statement: The skull suggests Indosaurus may have had horns over its eyes, although all fossil evidence has since been lost.
facts.quote: El cráneo sugiere que el Indosaurus puede haber tenido cuernos sobre sus ojos, aunque toda la evidencia fósil se haya perdido desde entonces.

facts.statement: Indosaurus was originally assigned to Allosauridae but is now considered a member of the Abelisauridae family.
facts.quote: Originally assigned by Huene to the Allosauridae, Indosaurus is today considered a member of the Abelisauridae family.

facts.statement: Indosaurus is now considered a member of the Abelisauridae family, despite being originally assigned to Allosauridae.
facts.quote: Originalmente asignado por Huene a Allosauridae, Indosaurus se considera hoy un miembro de los Abelisauridae.

facts.statement: Indosaurus was related to the strange South American predator Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: Indosaurus estaba relacionado con el extraño predador sudamericano, Carnotaurus.

facts.statement: Indosaurus lived alongside sauropods such as Isisaurus and Jainosaurus, which it may have preyed upon.
facts.quote: It is known to have lived alongside sauropods like Isisaurus, Jainosaurus and the dubious Titanosaurus, which it may have preyed upon.

facts.statement: The Lameta Formation rocks where Indosaurus fossils were found were deposited in fluvial or lacustrine conditions.
facts.quote: The rocks of the Lameta formation appear to have been deposited in fluvial or lacustrine conditions.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists speculate that Indosuchus, Lametasaurus, and Indosaurus should be considered nomina dubia.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists have speculated that Indosuchus, Lametasaurus and Indosaurus should be considered as nomina dubia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Orthogoniosaurus is the same animal as Indosaurus but based on different material.
facts.quote: Orthogoniosaurus puede ser el mismo animal pero basado en diferente material.

facts.statement: The time range for Indosaurus is estimated from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The environment where Indosaurus lived has alternatively been considered semi-arid or tropical humid.
rejected.quote: The environment at the time of deposition has alternatively been considered semi-arid, or tropical humid.
